$comment: Synth-claims config for the Aspen (NPI 1900000007) incident-to calibration. The original CALIBRATION-5B2E14D2 v3 run was driven by these exact values — preserving them here as the first generalized config means the refactored engine produces byte/row-equivalent output, and the pinned v3 case state remains reproducible.

scheme.$doc: Scheme injection: a fraction of subject's ESTABLISHED + NEW-patient E&M claims are split from billed_under_npi (subject) into rendering_npi=<one of renderer_npis>. The 'fraud' is rendering != billed-under without the conditions of 42 CFR 410.26 being met. The intensity grows over the cutoff window. Enrollment-gating prevents pre-enrollment NP attributions.

1900000040.name: C. SCHANIE
1900000040.$comment: Real NPPES enrollment date (verified via sandbox_nppes 2026-06-05)

scheme.$co_located_doc: Real co-located providers at 4010 Dupont Cir per address_sweep. These get fully-disaggregated REAL panel rows (no scheme injection) — they ARE the within-building control the agent uses to argue the scheme is subject-specific, not practice-wide.

intensity_by_year.$doc: Per-year fraction of subject's billed-under E&M that is NP-rendered. Ancillary codes (labs, vaccines, G-codes) are always rendered by the subject (MD) — share=0.

compliant_background.$doc: ~30% of peers run COMPLIANT incident-to via a randomly-paired real KY NP. Within those peers, 22% of established E&M claims have rendering != billing. This makes 'rendering != billed-under' a normal pattern in the data (not a fraud label), so the agent must use SCHEME-PROFILE evidence to conclude the subject is the outlier.
